threat_event: Attacker signs in to the RMM tool with a shared support account and pushes a malicious script to managed customer servers, including both banks' servers
threat_source: Cybercriminal group targeting managed service providers
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 2 shared support accounts whose password and MFA seed sit in the team vault; password not changed after a departure until 2026-07-23; console open to any internet address; no approval for multi-customer scripts; RMM logs kept 30 days and not monitored
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R05 (12 CFR 53.4(a)); Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.a and III.C.1.e (bank contracts); Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a)
existing_controls: MFA on named RMM accounts; EDR on staff laptops; MDR watches identity provider sign-ins
treatment_plan: Remove the shared accounts and rotate every RMM secret (first milestone 2026-10-15); restrict console sign-in to company addresses; turn on two-person approval for scripts aimed at more than one customer; export RMM logs to the MDR; add incident notice terms to the RMM contract

threat_event: Ransomware operator or destructive attacker with administrator access deletes customer VMs and every backup
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Cloud backup copy in the same account as the portal with no immutability; one administrator credential can reach the array, the appliance, and the cloud copy
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R05 (12 CFR 53.4(a)); Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.h (bank contracts)
existing_controls: Nightly backups with a 30-day cloud copy; VPN with MFA in front of the management network
treatment_plan: Move the backup copy to a separate cloud account with object lock (30 days); break-glass user stored offline; two-person approval for backup deletion; quarterly recorded restore tests

threat_event: Attacker with a stolen VPN credential uses the shared hypervisor administrator account to take over the cluster
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One shared local administrator account for all engineers; BMC passwords shared and unchanged since 2022; no MFA past the VPN; BMCs reachable by every VPN user
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R05 (12 CFR 53.4(a)); Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.a (bank contracts)
existing_controls: VPN with identity provider MFA; management VLAN not reachable from customer networks
treatment_plan: Named hypervisor manager accounts federated to the identity provider with MFA; BMCs reachable only from a jump host; rotate BMC passwords into the vault with per-person checkout

threat_event: Attacker exploits the internet-facing portal and uses its stored service credential to control every customer VM
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Portal service account has full administrator rights in the hypervisor manager; password in a plain-text configuration file; commercial portal software has had public vulnerabilities and is updated about 30 days after release
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.a (bank contracts)
existing_controls: HTTPS only; SSH limited to office and VPN addresses; the portal VM is not on the management network
treatment_plan: Limit the service account to the VM actions the portal needs; move the secret to the cloud secrets service; apply critical portal updates within 7 days; include the portal VM in monthly scans

threat_event: Credential stuffing takes over a customer portal administrator account and the attacker deletes or copies that customer's VMs
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Customer MFA optional (21% of administrators enrolled); no lockout or rate limit on the portal; support desk resets passwords on an email check alone
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.a (bank contracts)
existing_controls: Tenant separation in the portal; nightly backups for add-on VMs
treatment_plan: Turn on lockout and rate limits; require MFA for customer administrators (Bank A and Bank B first, by 2026-10-31); call-back check before any reset or console grant

threat_event: Attacker exploits an unpatched hypervisor or BMC vulnerability
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Hosts two minor releases behind; BMC firmware not updated since 2022; no internal vulnerability scanning
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines II.B.2 and III.C.3 (bank contracts)
existing_controls: Management network behind the VPN
treatment_plan: Monthly authenticated scans; KEV catalog tracking; host upgrade in the November maintenance window; quarterly BMC firmware cycle

threat_event: Former workforce member uses access that was never removed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No termination checklist; a former Support Engineer's VPN account stayed active until 2026-07-22 and he stayed on the colocation access list until 2026-08-18; the shared RMM password he knew was not changed until 2026-07-23
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.a and III.C.1.b (bank contracts)
existing_controls: VPN and identity provider MFA tied to the person's phone; colocation biometric entry
treatment_plan: Last-day checklist covering every system, the colocation list, and rotation of shared secrets; monthly account reconciliation by the Operations Manager

threat_event: Customer server passwords in the PSA vault are exposed through a staff account takeover or a breach at the PSA vendor
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Vault holds administrator passwords for managed customer servers, including bank servers, readable by all 7 staff
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.a (bank contracts); Fla. Stat. 501.171(2)
existing_controls: Vault encrypted at rest by the vendor; identity provider MFA
treatment_plan: Restrict vault folders by role; move bank server passwords to the business password manager with per-person access; rotate all bank server passwords

threat_event: Hurricane or site-wide failure takes DC-1 offline for days
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Single site; no second data center; only 145 of about 260 VMs have backups; restoring into the cloud tenant has never been tried
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R05 (12 CFR 53.4(a)); Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.h (bank contracts)
existing_controls: Colocation facility built for high winds with generator power (SOC 2 system description); nightly cloud backup copy
treatment_plan: Degraded-mode plan to restore add-on VMs into the cloud tenant, tested before the 2027 hurricane season; tell customers in writing which VMs it covers; price a replication tier

threat_event: Power or cooling failure at the colocation facility
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Single facility
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.h (bank contracts)
existing_controls: Redundant power feeds, generators, and cooling described in the provider's SOC 2 report; dual power supplies in every company device
treatment_plan: Accepted by the Owner: facility redundancy is evidenced in the SOC 2 report and the company cannot add more at this size; revisit with R-009

threat_event: Storage array failure or firmware defect takes down or corrupts every customer VM
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One storage array (dual controller) holds all VM disks; firmware updates applied ad hoc
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.h (bank contracts)
existing_controls: Dual controllers; next-business-day parts contract; nightly backups for add-on VMs
treatment_plan: Firmware updates through the change process after vendor release notes are checked; keep spare drives on site; recovery steps in the contingency plan

threat_event: An intrusion in the management plane goes undetected
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Hypervisor manager, BMC, RMM, cloud, and DNS logs not sent to the MDR; device logs roll over in about 7 days; nobody reviews logs
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.f (bank contracts)
existing_controls: MDR monitoring of laptops, identity provider, and firewalls
treatment_plan: Send RMM, cloud, hypervisor manager, and DNS logs to the MDR; keep them 12 months; weekly 30-minute review checklist

threat_event: The MDR's AI triage closes a true attack as benign, or automatically suspends the on-call engineer's account in the middle of an incident
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: AI triage auto-closes most alerts with no company review; automated containment thresholds set by the MDR without the company's input (P10)
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.f (bank contracts)
existing_controls: MDR analysts review escalated alerts
treatment_plan: No auto-close for alerts on privileged accounts and tooling; monthly sample review of auto-closed alerts; break-glass account excluded from automatic suspension; contract terms on telemetry use (see P10)

threat_event: Bank customers are not notified as soon as possible after an incident that disrupts their covered services for 4 hours or more
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No notice procedure until P08; Bank A's designated contact left the bank in 2024; Bank B never provided one; nobody owns the 4-hour determination
affected_asset_or_process: BP-05; Bank A and Bank B services
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R05 (12 CFR 53.4(a)); Interagency Guidelines Supplement A (bank contracts)
existing_controls: Owner knows both banks' executives
treatment_plan: Collect and verify designated contacts from both banks; 4-hour determination step at the 2-hour mark in P08; quarterly contact check; tabletop with a bank scenario

threat_event: An untested change to the cluster or network causes a wide outage, or maintenance is not announced to a bank
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Changes announced in team chat only; no approval or rollback plan; maintenance mailing list misses Bank B, so the 53.4(b) exception may not apply
regulatory_driver: C-IT-R05 (12 CFR 53.4(b)); Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.d (bank contracts)
existing_controls: Experienced engineers; cluster tolerates one host down
treatment_plan: Change log in the PSA with second-engineer approval and rollback steps; maintenance notices to bank-designated contacts at least 5 business days ahead

threat_event: Phishing and repeated push prompts take over a staff sign-in account
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Push approval without number matching; no phishing simulations; one staff phishing click in 2026 was handled with no record
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.a and III.C.2 (bank contracts)
existing_controls: Identity provider MFA; MDR identity alerts with automatic account suspension
treatment_plan: Hardware security keys for all 7 staff; quarterly phishing simulations

threat_event: The Owner's standing administrator accounts are compromised
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Owner uses full administrator rights in the identity provider, cloud tenant, and RMM tool for day-to-day work, including email
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.a (bank contracts)
existing_controls: MFA on all three accounts
treatment_plan: Separate everyday and administrator accounts for the Owner; administrator rights only for planned tasks

threat_event: Security and recovery stall because one person holds the knowledge and the security role
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: The Lead Systems Engineer is the only person who has rebuilt the cluster and also runs security part-time
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.A.2 (bank contracts)
existing_controls: Shared runbook notes in the PSA
treatment_plan: Written recovery runbook; a Systems Engineer trained as backup; Owner reviews security work monthly

threat_event: A breach at the RMM, PSA, or MDR provider exposes the company's customers
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No vendor reviews; RMM contract has no incident notice terms; MDR contract allows telemetry use for model training
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.D.2 (bank contracts); Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a)
existing_controls: Vendors' own security programs (not reviewed)
treatment_plan: Yearly review of each critical vendor's SOC 2 report or questionnaire; incident notice of 72 hours or less in contracts at renewal

threat_event: A denial-of-service attack on one customer VM fills the shared uplinks at DC-1 and takes down every customer
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Shared bandwidth; basic upstream filtering only; no null-route procedure
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines II.B.2 (bank contracts)
existing_controls: Colocation upstream filtering; firewall rate limits
treatment_plan: Written null-route procedure with the colocation provider's NOC; quote for an on-demand scrubbing service

threat_event: Failed drives or retired hardware leave DC-1 with readable customer data
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Failed drives returned under warranty; array volumes not encrypted; no wipe records for retired hosts
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.C.4 (bank contracts); Fla. Stat. 501.171(8)
existing_controls: Engineers wipe retired hosts with the vendor tool
treatment_plan: Keep-the-drive warranty option; certified destruction with records; encryption at rest on new array volumes

threat_event: A customer VM is used for phishing or botnet activity and the company's address ranges are blocklisted
threat_source: Customer or attacker using a customer VM
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Self-service VMs; abuse reports handled by email
regulatory_driver: MSA acceptable use terms
existing_controls: Acceptable use terms; abuse mailbox checked daily; VMs can be suspended
treatment_plan: Accepted by the Information Security Lead: Low risk, and the abuse process has worked for three reports in 2026

threat_event: Lost or stolen laptop
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Laptops leave the office for on-call work
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.c (bank contracts)
existing_controls: Full-disk encryption; EDR; remote wipe; MFA
treatment_plan: Accepted by the Information Security Lead: Low residual risk; encrypted data is not personal information under Fla. Stat. 501.171(1)(g)2

threat_event: Attacker on the management network uses the backup appliance's default administrator password to delete local backups
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Vendor default password in use since installation (found in P07 testing on 2026-08-18); appliance reachable by every VPN user
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.a and III.C.1.h (bank contracts)
existing_controls: VPN with MFA; cloud copy of backups
treatment_plan: Password changed 2026-08-19; move the appliance to its own network segment; check all devices for default passwords

threat_event: Loss of control of the DNS provider account leaves about 190 customer zones unrecoverable
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One administrator account with its MFA seed in the shared vault; no zone export outside the provider
regulatory_driver: Interagency Guidelines III.C.1.h (bank contracts)
existing_controls: MFA on the account
treatment_plan: Nightly zone export to the backup copy; named administrator accounts with personal MFA
